> **These notes are unfinished intentionally.** We have covered the first two parts in detail. Later parts will be documented when we actually reach them.

## N.I.C.E.

The working design cycle is:

**Needs & Necessities → Investigate & Inquire → Create & Communicate → Evaluate → repeat**

So far, our detailed work has focused on the first two stages.

## Needs & Necessities

Before choosing a solution, identify what the design actually needs to accomplish.

Useful questions include:

- Who is this for?
- What must it do?
- What restrictions matter?
- What would make it fail?
- What is necessary?
- What would only be nice to have?

A **need** describes something the design should accomplish.

A **necessity** is something that must be present or must be respected.

A **constraint** limits the solution. Time, cost, materials, safety, space, tools, and rules can all become constraints.

A **nice-to-have** may improve the design, but the design can still succeed without it.

[Open the Needs & Necessities slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TX9yMuScKH04QcF0TBzkMZTycqwOfSDpK0wZtJ-EbJQ/edit?usp=drivesdk)

## Investigate & Inquire

Research should begin with a question, not with a search box.

Our working sequence is:

**Ask → Search → Compare → Improve**

Before searching, use the needs you already identified.

Then:

1. find existing solutions
2. compare at least two
3. check whether they meet the actual needs
4. notice what each solution does well or poorly
5. use that evidence to improve your own idea

[Open the Inquiry slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1FoN2vg_Tmm2QAUfiJSqPqeSmV7y_m5Brknn0JXxKv0s/edit?usp=drivesdk)
